answer.answer:
Concrete becomes circular by two moves that the record documents: design the connections to be reversible rather than glued or monolithic, so elements can be taken apart and recovered, and attach component-level data, material passports, to those elements so recovery and reuse are economically worth doing. Traceable data is the single documented requirement for circular construction and is drawn on by 26 of the 50 coded cases, three times as many as circular construction itself at 8, so the data layer is in place far more often than the circular intent that would use it; the documented payoff on the other side is material and energy saving and reduced CO2 and waste. Note also that traceable data cuts investment uncertainty, which matters because cost uncertainty is one of the things that most often travels with circular projects. Nothing in the material in front of me is specific to concrete work as such, and no deployed project or census record for circular construction appears here, so this rests on the literature rather than on a built case.

**The mechanism, end to end**

Circular construction/DfDisAssembly (VA15) is a Value in the ontology [1], and it carries exactly one inbound and one outbound dependency edge in the whole graph, so what follows is the complete documented path.

Upstream, the requirement: Allow traceable/linked data (VA9) enables Circular construction/DfDisAssembly (VA15), because component data and material passports make recovery and reuse economically viable [2]. This is backed by peer-reviewed evidence, and 5 of the 50 coded cases carry both ends of it. For concrete specifically, the binding constraint named in the record is jointing: circular construction enables Material/energy saving/reduce CO2/waste (VA4), on the mechanism that glued and monolithic joints limit salvage potential while reversible connection design under DfDisAssembly enables material recovery [3]. Monolithic casting is precisely what makes conventional concrete non-recoverable, so this edge is where the practical instruction sits: cast or precast to a reversible connection detail. That edge is peer-reviewed and carried by 6 of the 50 cases.

Third, the economics: Allow traceable/linked data (VA9) mitigates Increase cost/investment uncertainty (RI3), on the reasoning that material passports reduce uncertainty about the circular potential and economics of disassembled elements, peer-reviewed and carried by 7 of the 50 cases. Those two, DEP69 and DEP70, are the only outbound edges VA9 carries.

**What tends to sit alongside it, as correlation not cause**

The enablers most often co-occurring with VA15 across cases are Material testing (PR10, weight 8), Integrate supply chain (VA14, weight 7), Modularisation (PR5, weight 6), Excavation/transportation (PR16, weight 6), Early contractor involvement (CO11, weight 6), DfMA for DFAB process (PR9, weight 6), Increase cost/investment uncertainty (RI3, weight 6), Design engineer (AC3, weight 5), Bespoke/customised design (AT1, weight 5), Subtractive manufacturing (PR7, weight 4), CNC machines (RE7, weight 4) and Increase material usage/waste (RI16, weight 3) [4]. These are 12 of 125 co-occurring enablers in total [4], a ranked cut and not a complete set, and none of them is asserted as a cause of circularity. Read as a profile rather than a recipe, they suggest circular work in the record tends to be modular, designed with the fabricator early, and validated by material testing, but the graph asserts no dependency on any of them.

**What the record does not give**

There is no Concrete work enabler in the material retrieved, so the widening from concrete construction to circular construction generally means this answer cannot claim anything specific to cast-in-place or precast concrete beyond the joint-reversibility mechanism just quoted. The only place concrete appears explicitly is on a different question: Additive manufacturing (PR3) depends on Regulatory/legal concern (RI18), because 3D printed concrete walls require certification against acceptance criteria for structural strength, fire safety and durability [5], evidence graded as standard and carried by 2 of the 50 cases. That is a route to printing concrete, not to recovering it.

No Process RP record or CensusProcess record for circular construction, and no firm, appears in this context, so I cannot name a deployed line or site that did this. Take the three edges above as the documented path and the rest as untested in the coded record.
